The RHP is out for the Jio IPO.

Most of us use digital services every day.

But how often do we look at the business figures behind them?

The Jio Platforms issue materials disclose some numbers that help put the scale of its operating business into perspective.

As of June 30, 2026:

• 533.3 million customers in India
• 284.9 million 5G customers
• 28.6 million fixed broadband subscribers

And there’s more to understand beyond customer numbers.

For FY2026, the disclosed financial figures include:

• Revenue from operations: ₹1,46,885.3 crore
• EBITDA: ₹76,255.4 crore
• EBITDA margin: 51.91%

These are historical figures reported in the issue materials, not predictions of future performance.

Here’s the distinction worth remembering:

Being a customer of a company and becoming a shareholder are two very different things.

Using a service is part of everyday life. Evaluating an investment requires looking at the company’s financials, the terms of the issue, and the risks disclosed in its offer document.

Those risks matter, too. The issue materials identify areas including spectrum and licensing, dependence on the operating subsidiary, network disruption, technology, and cybersecurity.

Big numbers can tell us about business scale.

But understanding a company means looking at the complete picture—not just the numbers that stand out.

Read the offer document and consider the disclosures carefully before drawing your own conclusions.
